**Tier 4** — decisions — policies, overrides, scenarios · owned by `engine` · `public.scenario_templates`

**One row is** One shipped starting point for a scenario: a named disruption shape with its schedule, its suggested playbook and the run settings that go with it. A template is not a scenario — applying one WRITES a scenario, and the two diverge from that moment.

## Uniqueness

| Columns | Source | Constraint |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | column PRIMARY KEY | `scenario_templates_pkey` |
| `slug` | column UNIQUE | `scenario_templates_slug_key` |

## Constraints

These reject the row outright. A value that fails one of them does not arrive
partially or get corrected — the write fails.

|---|---|---|
| `scenario_templates_category_check` | `CHECK (category IN ('supplier','logistics','demand','production','geopolitical'))` | `20260609000022_scenario_templates.sql` |
| `scenario_templates_severity_check` | `CHECK (severity IN ('low','medium','high','extreme'))` | `20260609000022_scenario_templates.sql` |

## Governance

| | |
|---|---|
| Read capability | any project member |
| Write capability | **no user-facing write path** |
| Minimum project role | `editor` |
| Tier transitions audited | yes |
| Row-level security | enabled |
| Policies on the table | 1 — all carry a predicate |

Tier 4 — the DECISION plane: what a person or an agent CHOSE, as against the dataset they chose it over and the result it produced. `result-binding` (I8) needs all three, which is why WP 6.3 keeps the results and this package takes the decisions. Audited from WP 6.4: the three statement-grain triggers land beside this sidecar, because `dataPlaneAudit.test.ts` scopes its rule to tables IN the contract and a deferred table's writes are unaudited with nothing to notice (D54). **Every row is a system row (`is_system` defaults true) and there is no user-facing write path**, so `write` is null and the audit triggers guard a table only a migration changes — which is the point: a change to the shipped catalog is exactly the kind of change nobody notices. **Six of the seven presets name a disruption target the mapper cannot resolve (§4 D112)**, so a run from one of them completes with the disruption ABSENT rather than failing, and that is the open question this package carries.

`CSV header` is the name the **user types**, which is not always the column name —
that gap is defect D21. A dash means the column has no CSV origin.

| Column | CSV header | Type | Unit | Required in CSV | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` 🔑 | — | `uuid` | — | — | Surrogate key. |
| `slug` | — | `text` | — | — | The template's stable name, UNIQUE across the catalog. What a preset is cited by. |
| `name` | — | `text` | — | — | What a person reads. |
| `description` | — | `text` | — | — | One sentence on the scenario it sets up. Defaults to the empty string rather than NULL. |
| `category` | — | `text` | — | — | Which family of disruption this is. Free text with no vocabulary table behind it, so a typo creates a category rather than failing — the same shape `disruption_scenario_settings.key` carries (§16 · WP 6.4 slice 13). |
| `severity` | — | `text` | — | — | How hard the shipped version of this scenario hits. A label on the template, not a parameter the engine reads. |
| `icon` | — | `text` | — | — | The glyph the picker draws. NULL where none was chosen. |
| `disruption_schedule` | — | `jsonb` | — | — | THE DECISION SHAPE — the events, their timing and their targets, copied into a scenario when the template is applied. **This is where D112 lives**: six of seven name a target `_map_events` cannot resolve. |
| `suggested_playbook_name` | — | `text` | — | — | The recovery playbook this scenario is usually paired with, BY NAME rather than by id. A name is not a join key (G1) and this one is resolved at apply time, so a renamed playbook silently stops matching — recorded here rather than fixed, because the fix is a decision about what a suggestion IS. |
| `horizon_days` | — | `integer` | — | — | How long the shipped run covers, in days. The scenario gets its own copy and may be changed after. |
| `warmup_days` | — | `integer` | — | — | How much of that horizon is discarded before measurement. |
| `replications` | — | `integer` | — | — | How many replications the shipped version runs. |
| `seed` | — | `integer` | — | — | The root seed, so two people applying the same template get the same draws. |
| `is_system` | — | `boolean` | — | — | TRUE for every row today. The column exists so a user template could be told apart from a shipped one, and nothing writes a user template. |
| `created_at` | — | `timestamp with time zone` | — | — | When the row was created. Server-stamped. |
